newsitem.title: USA: Banc One card acquisition seen as good fit.
newsitem.headline: Banc One card acquisition seen as good fit.

text.p: Banc One Corp's proposed $7.3 billion acquisition of credit card issuer First USA Inc has the potential to produce a big return, analysts said Monday.

Columbus, Ohio-based Banc One is already a major player in credit cards, and the merger will boost its credit card portfolio to $35 billion, said Robert Bonelli, executive vice president at Ernst & Co.
"It also gives them a tremendous amount of power in writing new business, particulary asset-backed securities" where the card portfolio is securitized and sold in the third market, he said.
"I wouldn't be looking at the combination squeezing out expenses. Instead, I would look at the degree of critical mass that will allow them to do a large amount of new business," Bonelli said.
"It's a good deal, it's an exciting deal. There is going to be a lot of value for shareholders going forward."
Banc One's share price slipped 3-3/8 to 41-3/4 in early trading. The decline was partly due to concerns about earnings dilution as a result of the merger.
Analyst George Salem of Gerard Klauer Mattison estimated diluton would be about four percent, but he stressed he had not yet had a briefing from Banc One.
Analysts agreed that Banc One was paying a steep price for First USA -- more than six times book value of about $8.50 a share, and more than 20 times earnings.
First USA shareholders will receive 1.1659 shares of Banc One for each First USA share, valuing First USA stock at $52.61, based on Friday's closing price for Banc One shares.
Analysts said well-publicized problems in credit card lending, mainly rising rates of delinquency and charge-offs, do not detract from the profitability of the business.
Nancy Bush of Brown Brothers Harriman said profitability in cards is about twice that in banking generally.
Bonelli said that while charge-off ratios have been creeping upward, "consumers are managing their credit today better than ever before."
With credit card interest rates at around 13.5 percent for the most creditworthy borrowers, and 16-17 percent for many people, the card business produces strong returns, he said.

A key measure of profitiabilty in the banking industry, return on equity, is over 20 percent in card lending, Bonelli said. For banks generally, return on equity has begun to rise to 18-20 percent after being stuck at 14-16 percent for a long time.
First USA is one of four large "monoline" credit card companies that have made card lending their main business. Stocks of the other three rose in sympathy with First USA.
Advanta Corp was up 4-1/2 to 47-5/8 at midday, Capital One Financial Corp was up 3-7/8 to 37-3/8, and MBNA Corp was up 1-3/8 to 32-1/2.
Bush said Capital One has unique operating methods that a buyer might find attractive, while MBNA has a large shareholder who seems happy with the investment.
